renovations.what: Two additions by the Center for Coastal and Ocean Mapping (offices, labs)
New ocean engineering wing from a $3M alumnus gift: four research labs, instrumentation lab, machine shop, 90-seat lecture hall, seminar room, covered outdoor workspace
Full-scale sediment flume installed beside the wave/tow tank

facts.text: Constructed in 1996 and dedicated October 10, 1997 for Jere A. Chase (class of 1936), a longtime UNH administrator who helped found the marine program.
The high bay holds a 60 x 40 x 20 ft deep engineering tank and a 12 x 8 x 120 ft wave/tow tank with a hydraulic wavemaker.
The high bay is a warehouse-like workspace with two interior bays and one exterior bay, home to the ASV lab and ROV refits.
A faculty member called the building "deceiving" from outside; the core high bay and some offices were built in the early 1990s.
It houses the Center for Coastal and Ocean Mapping.

verdict: Plain brick wings hide a cavernous high bay with deep engineering and wave/tow tanks, the real heart of UNH ocean engineering.
notes: No licensed exterior photo. Licensed interiors: a 2013 CCOM visualization lab (dropped acoustic-tile ceiling, fluorescent panels, no windows visible) and an older NOAA PD image of the tow tank in a tall industrial high bay with painted block walls. Archives exterior (1997) shows plain low brick wings. TNH 2017 says original lab built 1994; archives says 1996. 2017 wing size (12,000 sq ft) from search excerpt only.
judgeNotes: Exterior from 1997 archives photo: low plain brick. Interior photos show the tow tank and a windowless vis lab. Gallery leads with the tank since there is no licensed exterior.
